utterances.text: That's -- would it be appropriate if you start with one tomorrow and try to finish with just that witness and postpone the evidence -- the testimony of the second of these two witnesses till after Monday? Would that cause too much of a problem to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't cause any problem at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because that way you are guaranteed that -- you're guaranteed of starting with Mr. McLeod --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- straight away --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- as early as possible, after having spoken to him, and we can take it up from there. And then Monday -- Friday we can have part -- we can sit part in the morning or the whole day if you want to. I mean, I'm prepared to concede you even that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it depends also on the Defence teams. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think if we were to sit -- can I ask this, that whatever breaks are required -- the Milosevic trial has been sitting 9.30 till 4.30 with the breaks. If I could ask, say, that we could start at 11.00 on Friday morning with Mr. McLeod. That would give me enough time to speak to him in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would that be okay with the two Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely, Mr. President. But I have another problem. I spoke to Mr. Ackerman, and we agreed that Mr. Ackerman would start with the cross-examination first. According to what we have agreed on, it's quite clear that I won't be conducting the cross-examination on Friday but on Monday, so I can't prepare it now for -- for Friday. It's impossible. I could be here throughout Friday, but the cross-examination of this witness, I think I -- I would like you to agree to allow me to cross-examine this witness on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very grateful. I mean, that would be the best solution, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But Monday, that would be in the afternoon, not in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. That -- yes, that's all right. I can -- because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He would have finished -- he would have finished his examination-in-chief --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I would have hoped he could have finished everything if we sit all day Friday. As I say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But you still have the problem of Madam Fauveau not being prepared to cross-examine him on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, well, no, I would ask -- I'm sorry. I missed that. I wasn't listening that carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the whole --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, that causes -- the only thing -- the only way this can work - sorry, this will work - is if by sitting the lengthier time all cross-examination is completed. Your Honour, today is Wednesday. I -- with the greatest respect, I would have thought that either Mr. Zecevic or Madam Fauveau could have been ready to cross-examine Mr. McLeod - all they've got is one short witness. There's no dispute about the killing - tomorrow -- on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Obviously I will make an effort. But I have my lead counsel who has just arrived in this case and I have more work now than I had a week ago, and I really don't see how I could prepare for three witnesses in two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I suggested to Ms. Korner -- because sometimes you underestimate that I have passed through these in the past. This is why I suggested to you to forget about the second of these three witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I was going to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of these two witnesses, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And stick to one. That way you don't have to cross-examine the second witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. No. We're going to, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But -- yes, obviously. It's already been prepared for and these are witnesses who are -- they're not very lengthy witnesses. I'm sure that you saw the quantity of statements of Witness 7.62. I think there are two --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... there's no misunderstanding so that nobody getting bogged down --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- two binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Charles McLeod's previous transcripts. He has testified twice before but on wholly different areas of Bosnia. The only reason he is being called in this case is to deal with effectively his visit to Manjaca at the end of August and a little bit before he left. That is the only evidence on which -- he's never testified about this before. He kept a diary. Those parts of the diary which are relevant to the evidence he's going to give are quite short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let's -- let's sleep over it and perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you find time, some time tomorrow morning, you can discuss it between yourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. I'm just merely -- the reason I came in - we're still sitting - is -- I should inform Judge Schomburg that there's no change of courts necessary. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, not for the time being because it -- if that causes -- changing the schedule causes a problem to any one of the two Defence teams, obviously I have to take that into consideration and that comes first.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay? So we'll take it up again tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime just try to -- Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may have something to contribute, but I'd prefer to contribute it in the morning after I have a chance look at some things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Thank you. [Microphone not activated] So the case stands adjourned till tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m. -- this courtroom? This courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 6.36 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of June, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
